segments.text_original:
GSDP contribution in National GDP
Note – The Finance Minister began the budget speech with a pack of lies attempting to find excuses for his Government’s failure to implement the commitments made to the people of the State at the time of the elections. He alleged that, owing to the policies of the YSRCP, the economy of the State was in shackles. 
However, facts convey a very different picture. The contribution of the State to the National GDP was higher during the period of the YSRCP Government, indicating that the economy had strengthened during the period of the YSRCP Government.

Power Sector liabilities and losses
Financial support to sector 2014-19
Rs. 13,255 Crores
Financial support to sector 2019-24
Rs. 47,800.92 Crores
Note – During the presentation of the Budget, the FM alleged that the power sector suffered due to the policies of the YSRCP Government. However, the facts convey a different image.
 Accumulated losses of DISCOMs have risen to phenomenal levels during the period of the TDP Government and the debt has also grown during the period of the TDP Government at disproportionately high level. 
Is this a reflection of the TDP’s efficiency?
This resulted from under-release of subsidy to the DISCOMs, execution of PPAs at exorbitant tariffs and so forth during the TDP regime.

segments.text_original:
Capital Expenditure
The capital expenditure incurred during the first six months of this financial year is only Rs. 4,613.61 crores. The budget documents estimate the capital expenditure for the entire year at Rs. 32,712.84 crores. Which means, for the second six months of this financial year an amount of Rs. 28,099.23 crores of capital expenditure has to be incurred. Is this possible? Further, the budget documents suggest that, the amount estimated to be received as Central Assistance for Capital Expenditure is Rs. 12,950 crores. The amount budget by Central Government for all States is Rs. 1,50,000 crores. In this case, can we expect to receive such high share?
